newsitem.title: INDIA: Bombay shares end near day's high, index up 2.5 pct.
newsitem.headline: Bombay shares end near day's high, index up 2.5 pct.

text.p: Share prices staged a smart rally on Bombay bourses on Thursday, with the benchmark Bombay index jumping 71 points after falling over five percent in the last three sessions, traders said.
The market rose on a long-awaited technical recovery helped by unconfirmed newspaper reports of the government taking a more serious view of improving confidence in the bourses.
"It seems as if panic bells are ringing in New Delhi," said a broker who did not wish to be quoted. "The unabated fall in prices is making the government take note of the markets," the broker added.

The Economic Times newspaper on Thursday reported that top level finance ministry officials were likely to meet heads of major domestic financial institutions in New Delhi on Friday to "review the prevailing sluggish market conditions."
This week, the Bombay share index dived to a three-year low falling 145.44 points, or 5.03 percent in three sessions over last Friday's close of 2,890.50.
On Thursday, the index ended just off the day's high of 2,822.50 at 2,815.82, gaining 70.76 points or 2.58 percent over Wednesday's close.
Pivotals, Gujarat Ambuja Cement, L&T and auto stocks - TELCO M&M and Bajaj Auto which had been hammered in recent sessions stood out among the day's top gainers on short-covering.

Traders said foreign funds were also select buyers in the market, but domestic institutions stayed away. The 50-stock National Stock Exchange (NSE) index was up 17.38 points or 2.21 percent at 805.38 provisional close.

SBI rose 5.50 rupees to 210.75 rupees, TISCO 4.50 to 151.75, Reliance 5.25 to 183.50, ACC 25.70 to 945.75, ITC 8.75 to 271.0, Bajaj Auto 39.0 to 749.50, M&M 20.70 to 294.0, TELCO 16.0 to 311.0 and Gujarat Ambuja 16.70 to 212.0 and L&T 9.0 to 198.75.
